overview: Cobwebs strung between whatever holds them, and spiders that throw webs and spin new ones.

1.0.0: A cobweb held on two or more sides, by walls, floors, posts or more web, is drawn strung between them: a sheet across a corner, or one web carried on into the next.

Now and then a spider hunting something five to fourteen blocks off rears back and throws a ball of web trailing a strand of silk, which leaves a cobweb where it lands that comes apart five seconds later.

Now and then an idle spider turns its back to somewhere dark it can string a web across and spins one, strands of silk shooting from it to whatever the web will hang from, beside a web already there when it can, until the place around it has eight.
Spiders come in sizes: most smaller than before and no two alike, cave spiders still the smaller kind, and about one in twenty five a big one that is slower and takes two and a half times the hits.
